DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City JAN HON. RONALD T. GO Vice-Mayor Gerona, Tarlac Dear Vice Mayor Go. wwvv.ciii cv. h NO. II This pertains to your letter dated November 19, 2023 requesting this department's opinion on the propriety of the construction of a commercial building within the Municipal Hall Compound in the Municipality of Gerona, Tarlac. Per your representation, an allocation of public funds in the amount of Php 14,918,360 was made for the construction of said commercial building with an original approved budget of 15 million pesos. The same was allegedly questioned prompting your office to submit the following queries: 1. Whether or not the passage and approval of 2023 budget where an item is included for the construction of a commercial building within the Municipal Building within the Municipal Hall Compound with a project cost of Fifteen Million Pesos (Php 15,000,000.00) is for public purposes or private purposes? 2. Whether or not the purpose of constructing a particular commercial building using public funds of our municipality is a violation of Section305 (b) and Section 335 of R.A. 7160? 3. Whether or not there is a need to reclassify first the lot where our former police station is located as patrimonial property of our municipality before the same can be used by our LGU to generate resources or income? 4. Whether or not Section 18 of R.A. No. 7160 is applicable in the ongoing construction of commercial building using public funds of our municipality? 5. Whether or not there is a need to stop first the ongoing construction of the subject commercial building while waiting for the answer of your good office on all the issues that we presented. We find all the above queries interrelated; thus, we address the same simultaneously with the herein-below discussion. At the outset, let it be settled that the issue of whether a local government's undertaking is for a public purpose or not depends on the purpose delineated by the authority conferred thereon by the local legislative body. We clarify further that Philippine jurisprudence has expanded the definition of "public use" to include that which is for the advantage or for the benefit of the general public. This was explained in Republic of the Philippines vs. Heirs of Saturnino Q. Borbon and Court of Appealsl. To wit: I G.R. No. 165354; January 12, 2015. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Public use, in common acceptation, means "use by the public." However, the concept has expanded to include utility, advantage or productivity for the benefit of the public. (Emphasis Supplied) Verily, the fact that the building to be constructed is a commercial building does not alone suffice to conclude that public funds allocated therefor, and the land over which the building is being constructed, are already converted to private use. We are reminded that local governments, in the nature of being public corporations, are allowed to engage in proprietary activities through its revenue-raising power pursuant to Section 129 of R.A. No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991" (LGC): SECTION 129. Power to Create Source of Revenue - Each local government unit shall exercise its power to create its own sources of revenue and to levy taxes, fees, and charges subject to the provisions herein, consistent with the basic policy of local autonomy. Such taxes, fees, and charges shall accrue exclusively to the local government units. (Emphasis Supplied) The LGC's Section 16, on general welfare, and Section 18, on power to generate and apply resources, equally apply. It is therefore, this department's opinion that so long as the commercial building will be actually used for the local government's proprietary and revenue-raising capacity, the same does not cease to serve its public purpose as the benefits derived therefrom will still redound to the general public. On the issue of whether there is a need to reclassify the land, the same may be best addressed by the Land Registration Authority (LRA) considering its mandate and expertise on matters pertaining to Property Registration Decree and the Public Land Act; hence, we will defer to its authority in answering the same. This opinion is being issued based solely on the representation you submitted and it is without prejudice to contrary opinion and/or decisions of competent authorities as well as that of proper courts. We hope to have addressed your concern. Very truly yours, Y AU ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: N VI TOR R.
